premise: night shift at a gas station
scenes: The fluorescent ceiling panels hum faintly over the register as a raccoon carefully nudges the automatic sliding doors open with its snout. It trots down the candy aisle, makes direct eye contact from behind a display rack, and sets a crumpled twenty-dollar bill on the floor.

Through the rain-streaked front window, a vintage muscle car pulls up to pump four with its headlights off and engine purring in the dark. The driver's door swings open into the empty night, revealing a duffel bag zip-tied shut on the front passenger seat and nobody behind the wheel.

The coffee maker in the corner finishes brewing with a loud hiss, sending steam billowing across the quiet, linoleum-tiled floor. An old man in a bright yellow raincoat steps up to the counter and sets down a dripping wet, antique nautical compass right on top of the scratch-off lottery tickets.

Looking down aisle three of the brightly lit convenience store, where a raccoon sits beside a metal rack of chocolate bars, staring directly forward with a crumpled green twenty-dollar bill resting between its front paws.
